content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-19
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (Priority: P1)
14	
15	A user opens the chat and asks the AI agent something related to their life, without repeating what they already wrote elsewhere. The agent's answer reflects relevant things the user recorded before, not just the current message in isolation, and the exchange stays on screen as a normal, persisted conversation the user can come back to.
16	
17	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF04 — "memory" via semantic search over past entries. Without it, the screen is just a generic chat window with no connection to the rest of the product.
18	
19	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding an account with a prior entry about a specific topic, sending a chat message that references that topic without quoting it verbatim, and confirming the agent's response demonstrates awareness of the seeded entry's content.
20	
21	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
22	
23	1. **Given** the user has at least one prior entry about a specific topic, **When** they send a chat message related to that topic, **Then** the agent's response reflects information from that entry, even though the message itself never restated it.
24	2. **Given** a conversation already has one or more exchanges, **When** the user leaves the screen and returns later (including after an app restart), **Then** the full exchange history is still present, in the same order, without needing to be resent.
25	3. **Given** the user sends a chat message, **When** the message is accepted, **Then** it is stored and displayed as part of the conversation but does **not** create a journal entry — chat messages are conversational only, with no automatic persistence as an entry (the one exception, an explicit save action, belongs to a later unit and is out of scope here).
26	
27	---
28	
29	### User Story 2 - Always knowing what the agent is doing (Priority: P1)
30	
31	While waiting for or reading a response, the user can always tell, at a glance, which of three things is happening: the answer is still arriving, it finished successfully, or it failed — and a response that stops arriving partway through never just vanishes.
32	
33	**Why this priority**: RF04's acceptance criteria explicitly require these three states and the no-disappearing-partial-message rule; without a clear, honest status, users cannot trust the chat enough to rely on it.
34	
35	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by sending a message and observing the UI progress through the "processing/streaming" state into either "complete response" or "error," and separately by forcing a connection drop mid-response and confirming the partial text stays visible with a failure indication instead of disappearing.
36	
37	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
38	
39	1. **Given** the user has just sent a message, **When** the agent begins producing a reply, **Then** the response is revealed progressively (streaming) with a visible in-progress indicator, distinct from a finished message.
40	2. **Given** a response finishes streaming normally, **When** the last token arrives, **Then** the message is shown in its final, complete form with its timestamp, no longer carrying any in-progress indicator.
41	3. **Given** the connection drops, or the backend returns an error, while a response is still arriving, **When** that happens, **Then** whatever text had already arrived stays visible, together with a clear failure indication in place of the timestamp — the message is never removed or left in an ambiguous unfinished-looking state.
42	
43	---
44	
45	### User Story 3 - Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (Priority: P2)
46	
47	A response fails or is cut short. The user taps the failed message and gets a fresh attempt at an answer to the same question, without having to retype it, without creating a duplicate question in the history, and without disturbing the rest of the conversation.
48	
49	**Why this priority**: A direct extension of Story 2's failure state — the failure indication is only useful if there's a documented way out of it, and the requirement calls this out explicitly ("a way to try again" is part of RF04's own scope).
50	
51	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a response failure, tapping the failed message to retry, and confirming a new response is generated for the same original question, with the user's question appearing exactly once in the history.
52	
53	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
54

# Cerne Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Product Source of Truth
`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
this repository.

Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

### II. Fixed Technology Stack
The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```
The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.

Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.

## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)

These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:

- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
  loading indicator.
- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
  target.
- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
  80% test coverage.
- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
  `design_tokens.dart`.
- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).

## Scope & Delivery Boundaries

- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
  entry.
- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
    `design_tokens.dart`.
  - Implementing extension features.
  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.

**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.

**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
  redefinition.
- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
  guidance.
- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.

**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-11 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-11

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-17

- Q: The filter sheet's "TIPO DE ENTRADA" chips allow selecting more than one entry type at once, but both `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only a single `source` value per request, and every entry has exactly one `source` — so an entry can never match "every" selected type simultaneously. How should multiple selected entry-type chips be combined, and how should the request(s) be built? → A: Entries having ANY of the selected types are included (OR among the entry-type chips themselves), while that combined set is still ANDed with the active date range and search term. To build it, the app fires one request per selected entry type (each carrying the same `q`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`), merges the responses, de-duplicates by entry ID, and re-sorts the combined set (by relevance when a search term is active, otherwise reverse-chronological, matching RF07) before rendering — preserving the prototype's multi-select affordance without requiring a backend change. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: When the user is scrolled through a search result list (an active `q`) and nears the bottom, should the app try to load a further page, given `GET /entries/search` has no `cursor` parameter and caps results at `limit` (max 50)? → A: No — while a search term is active, the single fetch (up to `limit`) is the complete result set for that query; "scrollable" means scrolling within what is already loaded, not triggering a further fetch. Clearing the search text returns to `GET /entries`'s existing cursor-based infinite scroll (RF07) for filter-only or unfiltered browsing. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: With a 300 ms debounce and no server-side throttle on `GET /entries/search` (per its own API summary), could a slow, older response arrive after a newer request's response and overwrite it with stale results? → A: Yes, so the app MUST treat only the most recently fired request (per debounce fire, filter change, chip removal, or "Limpar filtros") as authoritative — discarding the response of any earlier, now-superseded request for the same screen state, never applying a late-arriving stale response over a newer one. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Finding an entry by what it means, not what it says (Priority: P1)

A user wants to find something they wrote about even though they can't remember the exact words they used. They type a term into the search bar on "Meus Registros" and get back entries that are about that topic, including ones that never use the literal word they typed.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF06 and the capability that sets this screen apart from a plain keyword filter — without it, the feature delivers no value beyond what RF07's list already provides.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding the three entries from `docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md` (none of which contains the literal search term) and confirming each documented search term (`ansiedade`, `cansaço`, `gratidão`) returns its matching entry.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the seeded entry that describes racing thoughts and a tight chest the night before a presentation (no occurrence of the word "ansiedade"), **When** the user searches "ansiedade", **Then** that entry appears in the results.
2. **Given** the user is typing a search term, **When** they type several characters in quick succession, **Then** exactly one search request is sent, 300 ms after they stop typing — not one request per keystroke.
3. **Given** the user clears the search text completely, **When** the field becomes empty, **Then** the screen returns to showing results based only on whatever filters are still active (or the full list, if none are active), without sending a search for an empty term.

---

### User Story 2 - Narrowing the list with filters (Priority: P1)

A user wants to see only entries from a particular date range and/or a particular capture method (text, audio, photo, chat), without necessarily typing any search term. They open the filter sheet, choose criteria, apply them, and see a narrowed list.

**Why this priority**: Equally core to RF06 as semantic search — the requirement explicitly treats "semantic similarity combined with metadata filters" as a single capability, and filtering alone (with no search text) must work correctly on its own.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the filter sheet on an account with entries of mixed dates and sources, applying a date range and an entry-type selection together, and confirming the result list contains only entries that satisfy both.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the filter sheet is open, **When** the user picks a date-range option (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês) and one or more entry-type chips (manual, áudio, foto, chat) and taps "Aplicar", **Then** the list narrows to entries that fall within the chosen date range AND have one of the chosen entry types — the date range and the entry-type selection are ANDed with each other, while multiple selected entry types are ORed among themselves (an entry has exactly one type, so it can never match more than one at a time).
2. **Given** the filter sheet's "CATEGORIA" chip group (trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), **When** the user taps one of those chips and applies the sheet, **Then** the result list is unaffected by that selection, because the backend has no category filter — the chips exist for visual fidelity to the prototype only.
3. **Given** the filter sheet is open, **When** the user taps "Limpar" inside the sheet, **Then** every selection in the sheet resets before it is applied.

---

### User Story 3 - Seeing and clearing what's currently applied (Priority: P2)

A user who has applied one or more filters, with or without a search term, wants to glance at the screen and immediately understand what is currently narrowing their results, and be able to remove any single criterion or all of them at once.

**Why this priority**: A usability layer on top of Stories 1 and 2 — the underlying narrowing already works without it, but the requirement's own acceptance criteria call out that filters must be clearable without restarting the screen, and the prototype dedicates a distinct state to this.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by applying two filters, confirming a chip appears for each with the funnel button shown filled, removing one chip and confirming only that criterion drops out, then using "Limpar filtros" and confirming the screen returns to its unfiltered list without reloading.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

### User Story 4 - Cached results stay trustworthy through a connectivity blip (Priority: P3)

A user is viewing search or filter results when the connection drops and later comes back. What they see while offline comes from the local cache, and once reconnected, the list reconciles with the server without showing the same entry twice or leaving stale results behind unnoticed.

**Why this priority**: A correctness property layered on top of Stories 1–3 rather than a feature of its own; it depends on search and filtering already producing a result list to keep consistent, and it protects against a subtle trust-eroding bug rather than blocking the core flow.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a search/filter result list, simulating a loss and restoration of connectivity, and confirming the list shown offline matches the cache, with no duplicated entries once the server is reachable again.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a search or filter result list is already loaded, **When** the device goes offline, **Then** the previously loaded results remain visible and scrollable from the local cache.
2. **Given** results were shown from cache while offline, **When** the connection is restored, **Then** the list reconciles with what the server currently returns for the same search/filter criteria, with every entry appearing exactly once (no duplicates).

### Edge Cases

- A search and/or filter combination matches zero entries on an account that does have entries: the screen shows a distinct "no results for this search/filter" message, not RF07's account-wide "Nenhum registro ainda" empty state, and offers a way to adjust or clear the applied criteria from there.

- A search request or a filtered fetch fails outright (timeout, malformed response, or the device is offline when the request would be sent): the screen shows a clear, retryable error without discarding whatever cached results are already displayed, and without attempting any write.
- The session expires while a search or a filtered view is active: the existing "Sessão expirada" overlay (RF07) handles it, and once resolved, the active search text and filters are still applied — they are not silently cleared by the session event.
- A filter is applied together with an active search term at the same time (not shown explicitly acting together anywhere in the prototype): both narrow the same result set together under AND logic, consistent with the requirement's general rule that "two or more filters applied at the same time narrow results with AND logic."
- A new search, filter change, or clear action fires while an earlier request for the same screen is still in flight: only the most recently fired request's response is ever applied to the screen; any earlier, now-superseded response is discarded so a slow stale response can never overwrite newer results.

lines: - **FR-005**: If the response stream is interrupted before completion (connection drop, backend error, or any other cause), the system MUST keep whatever partial text had already arrived visible, together with the failure indication — it MUST NOT remove, hide, or blank out a partial message.

- **FR-006**: A message in the error state MUST be tappable to trigger a retry (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`) that regenerates the response to that same original question. A retry MUST NOT duplicate the user's original question in the conversation, and MUST go through the same processing/streaming → complete/error states as any other response. Retrying MUST remain available after a retry itself fails, with no fixed limit on the number of attempts, and MUST remain available on any message in the error state regardless of how much later conversation exists after it.

- **FR-007**: While a response in the current conversation is streaming or sitting in the error state awaiting retry, the system MUST keep the message-send control disabled, re-enabling it only once that response reaches a final state (complete, or retried to a new resolution) — so a single conversation never has two responses in flight at once.
-- **FR-008**: The side menu MUST show a "CONVERSAS" section listing the user's existing conversations (`GET /chat/sessions`), each with its title and a timestamp.

- **FR-009**: The side menu MUST offer a "Novo Chat" action that opens the chat screen in an empty conversation state, ready to accept a first message, without discarding or altering any existing conversation. Selecting an existing conversation from the list MUST open it with its full message history intact, exactly as it was left.

- **FR-010**: A new conversation (`POST /chat/sessions`) MUST only be created at the point a first message is actually sent into an empty conversation state — opening an empty conversation state (via "Novo Chat," or on an account with no conversations yet) MUST NOT by itself create a session with no messages in it.

Sending MUST become possible again as soon as connectivity is restored, with no manual reset required.

content.content:
101	### Edge Cases
102	
103	- The user tries to send an empty or whitespace-only message: the send control stays disabled/inactive, and no request is made.
104	- A message at or near the backend's maximum length is sent: the system either prevents exceeding that maximum before sending or surfaces the backend's resulting validation error clearly, without losing the text the user typed.
105	- A message is sent while a previous response in the same conversation is still streaming, or is sitting in the failed/"tap to retry" state: the composer stays disabled until that turn resolves (completes or is retried to a new resolution), so a session never has two responses racing at once.
106	- The session expires (RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" behavior) while a response is mid-stream or while viewing history: the existing overlay is shown, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and once the user re-authenticates, the conversation resumes exactly where it was — this unit reuses that behavior rather than redefining it.
107	- The user navigates away from a conversation (e.g., via the side menu) while a response is still streaming: when the user returns to that conversation, the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded for it (complete or failed) rather than being stuck in a stale in-progress state tied to a connection that no longer exists.
108	- An account has zero conversations yet (first-ever use of chat): the chat screen still shows a ready-to-use empty conversation, and a session is created at the point the first message is actually sent.
109	- The user retries a failed message that is not the most recent message in the conversation: the retry still succeeds and only affects that specific message's response, leaving every later message in the conversation untouched.
110	- Opening the side menu's conversation list, the export job, dashboard, filters, action-plan board, and every other screen or action not named in this feature's scope: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.
111

- A message is sent while a previous response in the same conversation is still streaming, or is sitting in the failed/"tap to retry" state: the composer stays disabled until that turn resolves (completes or is retried to a new resolution), so a session never has two responses racing at once.
- The session expires (RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" behavior) while a response is mid-stream or while viewing history: the existing overlay is shown, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and once the user re-authenticates, the conversation resumes exactly where it was — this unit reuses that behavior rather than redefining it.

- An account has zero conversations yet (first-ever use of chat): the chat screen still shows a ready-to-use empty conversation, and a session is created at the point the first message is actually sent.
- The user retries a failed message that is not the most recent message in the conversation: the retry still succeeds and only affects that specific message's response, leaving every later message in the conversation untouched.

### User Story 5 - Reading history while offline (Priority: P3)

A user without a connection can still read everything they already loaded, but cannot send anything new, and is told clearly why.

**Why this priority**: Explicitly one of the four required prototype states for this screen, and it protects against the worse failure mode of a chat screen that looks broken or loses content when connectivity drops — but it is a secondary concern relative to the core conversation and failure-recovery loops above.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a conversation, simulating a loss of connectivity, confirming the existing history stays visible and scrollable, confirming the send control is disabled with an explanatory banner, and confirming sending is not possible until connectivity returns.

## Notes

- Per this repo's established precedent (specs 005/006), functional requirements reference the specific backend endpoints and screen/state names named in `docs/input/requirements.md` and the prototype extract directly, since those are frozen product inputs (Constitution Principle I) rather than implementation choices made by this spec.
- The one significant open design question for this unit — when a chat session is actually created on the backend, and which conversation the screen shows by default on open — was resolved as a documented default (see Assumptions) rather than left as a [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker: RF04's own description ("Continuous conversation") and `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title` both support lazy session creation and resuming the last-open conversation, with no equally reasonable competing default. All items pass; no spec updates required before `/speckit-clarify` or `/speckit-plan`.

content.content:
15:- Q: `POST /chat/sessions` accepts an optional `title`, the backend has no auto-titling logic of its own, and no endpoint exists to rename a session afterward — so whatever the app does at creation time is permanent for that conversation. Should the app send a title derived from the first message, or never send one? → A: The app derives a short title client-side from the first message's text (trimmed, capped to a short preview length) and sends it in `POST /chat/sessions`'s `title` field at the moment that first message creates the session. This is the only mechanism that can ever give a conversation a human-recognizable name, and User Story 4 explicitly requires the side menu to let users find past conversations "by name." (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16:- Q: `GET /chat/sessions` is cursor-paginated (`cursor`/`limit`, default 20, max 50) and its items carry no documented sort order; the prototype's side-menu extract shows a flat "CONVERSAS" list with no load-more control. How should the side menu order and page through sessions once an account has more than one page's worth? → A: The list is ordered by most recent activity (`lastUserMessageAt`, descending; a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed, since sessions are only created together with their first message), and the side menu fetches further pages via `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the "CONVERSAS" section (the same infinite-scroll pattern already established for RF07's own list) — so no conversation ever becomes unreachable as the account accumulates sessions beyond a single page. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
17:- Q: `docs/input/requirements.md` §6.3 marks both `GET /chat/sessions` and `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` as "works offline (cache)," without scoping that to only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped. Does offline mode cover every previously-opened conversation, or only the one open at disconnect? → A: The cache (and offline readability) covers every chat session the user has opened at least once while online — both the side menu's own session list and the message history of each previously-opened conversation remain browsable and switchable while offline; only creating a session, sending a message, and retrying require connectivity (already covered by FR-012). Selecting a conversation from the side menu that was never loaded while online, while currently offline, shows the standard no-connection state (no cached data to fall back to) rather than any content. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
75:**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by having at least one existing conversation, opening the side menu, confirming it lists past sessions with a title and timestamp, tapping "Novo Chat," confirming the chat screen shows an empty conversation, and confirming the prior conversation is unchanged when reopened from the list.
79:1. **Given** the user has one or more existing conversations, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** a "CONVERSAS" section lists each one with a title and a timestamp.
85:### User Story 5 - Reading history while offline (Priority: P3)
95:1. **Given** a conversation is already loaded, **When** the device goes offline, **Then** the existing message history remains visible and scrollable, and a banner explains that new messages are blocked.
96:2. **Given** the device is offline, **When** the user looks at the composer, **Then** the send control is visibly disabled — no message can be sent until the connection returns.
98:4. **Given** the user has previously opened more than one conversation while online, **When** the device goes offline and the user switches between those previously-opened conversations from the side menu, **Then** each one's cached history is shown exactly as it was left, not just the conversation open at the moment connectivity dropped.
111:- An account has more conversations than fit in one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` (more than its default/max `limit`): scrolling to the bottom of the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section fetches the next page via `cursor` rather than silently stopping at the first page.
112:- The user is offline and selects, from the side menu, a conversation that was never opened while online: no cached data exists for it, so the screen shows the standard no-connection state instead of any content, distinct from the normal offline case of browsing an already-cached conversation.
126:- **FR-008**: The side menu MUST show a "CONVERSAS" section listing the user's existing conversations (`GET /chat/sessions`), each with its title and a timestamp, ordered by most recent activity (latest `lastUserMessageAt` first). If the account has more sessions than fit in one backend page, the list MUST fetch further pages via the endpoint's `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the section, so every conversation stays reachable.
128:- **FR-010**: A new conversation (`POST /chat/sessions`) MUST only be created at the point a first message is actually sent into an empty conversation state — opening an empty conversation state (via "Novo Chat," or on an account with no conversations yet) MUST NOT by itself create a session with no messages in it. That creation call MUST include a `title` derived from the first message's own text (a short, trimmed preview), so the new conversation has a distinguishable, human-recognizable name in the side menu from the moment it exists — the backend has no auto-titling of its own and no later rename endpoint.
129:- **FR-011**: While the device is offline, the system MUST keep every previously-opened conversation's history, and the side menu's own "CONVERSAS" list, visible, scrollable, and switchable from the local cache — not only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped — MUST disable the send control, and MUST show an explanatory message that new messages are blocked until the connection returns. Selecting a conversation that was never opened while online, while currently offline, MUST show the standard no-connection state rather than any content, since nothing was ever cached for it. Sending MUST become possible again as soon as connectivity is restored, with no manual reset required.
130:- **FR-012**: The system MUST NOT attempt to create a new conversation or send/retry a message while offline — both actions require a connection and MUST be blocked client-side rather than attempted and failed.
136:- **Chat Session**: One conversation thread, identified by an id, with a title derived client-side from its first message at creation time and shown in the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section (a defensive generic placeholder is shown only if a session is ever encountered with an empty title), the persona that was in effect when it was created (read-only here — not user-editable in this unit), and timestamps including when it was created and when it last received a user message (the latter drives the side menu's ordering).
149:- **SC-006**: While offline, 100% of the history of every previously-opened conversation stays readable and switchable from the side menu (not only the one open at disconnect), and the send control is visibly disabled for the entire duration of the outage, re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning.
154:- A conversation ("session") is created lazily, only when the user actually sends a first message into an empty conversation state, rather than eagerly when "Novo Chat" is tapped or when the chat screen is simply opened — this keeps the backend free of empty sessions and matches `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title`. Re-opening the app resumes whichever conversation the user was last in (if any exist); when none exist yet, the screen shows the same empty, ready-to-send state "Novo Chat" also produces.
158:- Every chat session is created with a client-derived title (see FR-010), so the generic placeholder in the side-menu list is a defensive fallback for an unexpected empty title rather than the normal case; the exact wording of both the derived-title preview length and the fallback placeholder is a presentation detail left to implementation.

149:- **SC-006**: While offline, 100% of the history of every previously-opened conversation stays readable and switchable from the side menu (not only the one open at disconnect), and the send control is visibly disabled for the entire duration of the outage, re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning.
154:- A conversation ("session") is created lazily, only when the user actually sends a first message into an empty conversation state, rather than eagerly when "Novo Chat" is tapped or when the chat screen is simply opened — this keeps the backend free of empty sessions and matches `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title`. Re-opening the app resumes whichever conversation the user was last in (if any exist); when none exist yet, the screen shows the same empty, ready-to-send state "Novo Chat" also produces.
158:- Every chat session is created with a client-derived title (see FR-010), so the generic placeholder in the side-menu list is a defensive fallback for an unexpected empty title rather than the normal case; the exact wording of both the derived-title preview length and the fallback placeholder is a presentation detail left to implementation.
